Increased gut permeability
-
Decreased microbial diversity
-
Decreased fecal SCFA (Lafﬁn et al.,
2019; Montrose et al., 2021)
Soft drink and reﬁned sugar intake
increase CD risk (Narula et al., 2021)
Sugar intake had no impact on CD risk
(Racine et al., 2015)
Soft drink and reﬁned sugar intake
increase UC risk (Narula et al., 2021)
Sugar and soft drink intake as well as
sucrose intake are associated with
increased risk (Racine et al., 2015; Wang
et al., 2017)
Fat
-
Diet high in saturated fat increases
sulphite-reducing pathogens (Devkota
et al., 2012)
-
Diet high in animal fat (as well as sugar)
resulted in dysbiosis (increased pro
inﬂammatory organisms) and
decreased favorable SCFA (Agus et al.,
2015)
-
High animal fat diet decreased secretory
IgA (Muhomah et al., 2019)
-
Associations between total fat, animal
fat and n-6 PUFA and incidence of CD
(Shoda et al., 1996)
-
High n-3 PUFA and n-3:n-6 PUFA ratio
associated with lower risk of CD (Amre
et al., 2007)
-
Consumption of the n-3 PUFA, DHA
associated with reduced risk of UC
(John et al., 2010)
-
Linoleic acid (a n-6 PUFA) associated
with an increased risk of UC
(Tjonneland et al., 2009)
Recent meta-analysis showed no
association between fat total or subtype
intake and disease
